analysis.title: One And Done? Options Market Prices Seven Weeks Of Calm For Less Than One Day Of Chaos, Two Days Before Nvidia Reports
key_insights: Goldman's Brian Garrett says the cash market lacks conviction while the options market is highly convinced that the Nov 5 crash was an isolated event.
The S&P 500 year-end (Dec 31) at-the-money straddle costs 4.2% of the index, less than the 4.4% the S&P fell on Nov 5. The Nasdaq 100 year-end straddle costs 6.8% against a 6.4% fall that day.
The straddle breakevens are roughly 7,880 on the upside and 7,245 on the downside, based on Friday's close (the note's own math).

The gap between implied and realized vol is the widest in over a year. S&P one-month implied is about 8 points below realized, and the implied-realized spread is negative in every US sector except utilities.
S&P 10-day realized vol is near 30 while the daily move implied by variance swaps has dropped toward 1.2%. Goldman's Panic Index is rolling over while one-month realized stays near its highs.
Hedge funds sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1. Net exposure is in the 2nd percentile of the past five years.
Global single stocks have been sold for 9 straight weeks while index and ETF products were bought for four. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is the lowest in Goldman's data, which start in 2016.

Vol control and risk parity funds cut about $40BN of global equity exposure in a week. Goldman models show roughly another $27BN of SPX supply over the next few sessions. These funds re-risk if realized vol keeps falling.
Hedge fund net exposure is near five-year lows while retail equity exposure (AAII) through end of October was close to its highs.
Brent fell about 20% in seven sessions at the start of November. New longs are now arriving through futures and calls with oil in the mid-$90s.
Client behavior per Garrett: not buying calls (S&P call skew is flat while spot rallied), collaring, and shorting the VIX. VIX puts traded their highest 10-session volume of the year.
Collar detail: a 3-month put struck 10% below the market funds a call about 5.5% above it. The same put now funds two 3-month 108/118 call spreads.
Garrett's VIX trade is the December 18/16 1x2 put spread for about 0.50, with the relevant VIX future at 19.4. The note's napkin math gives a maximum payout of 3-to-1 at a December VIX settle of 16.
Nomura's Charlie McElligott argued last week that the VIX floor is now higher, around 18.
Goldman's Peter Callahan: NDX gained about 350bps and semis about 800bps last week, but both closed Friday below their 200-day moving averages.
US financial conditions are at their most restrictive in about 18 months after another hot CPI. The 10-year is at 5.15% and oil is heading toward $96.
Nvidia reports Tuesday 11/17 after the close. The stock is down 12% YTD, its market cap is below $4 trillion, its 14-day RSI is 24 (lowest since 2019), and it trades at 11x NTM P/E.

Consensus FY2028 GAAP EPS for Nvidia is a record of about $16.25 and the stock closed Friday at $162.85, roughly 10x that estimate. Callahan expects focus on Vera Rubin momentum, 2027+ visibility, gross margins and capital allocation.
Per the note, 14 banks are cutting Nvidia targets while keeping Buy ratings.
The S&P 500 excluding AI stocks is up about 17% over the past year against 12% for the index.
Palo Alto reports Wednesday after the close. It has traded lower on 9 of the last 12 prints, including a 9.3% drop last time, and options price a 9.4% move.
Disney is retesting the $120s, a level that has capped it for more than four years. Intuit has not closed above its 200-day moving average in more than a year.

Goldman 2027 outlooks: Hatzius 2.8% global growth, Oppenheimer expects the bull market to continue, commodities base case near zero index return after a 26% gain this year, and the capex team sees AI hardware and IP spending above $900BN by end-2026 and $1.4 trillion by end-2027, about 4% of US GDP.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol sellers treat Nov 5 as isolated. Implied vol is well below realized, the realized crash drops out of the 1-month window in early December, and VIX puts are in heavy demand.
tension_points.bear_case: The year-end straddle (4.2%) costs less than the Nov 5 move (4.4%), while the window includes Nvidia earnings, a December FOMC with a 50bp hike floated, and about $27BN of mechanical supply. Nomura's McElligott sees the VIX floor near 18.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another move like Nov 5 in either direction pays the entire year-end premium. The straddle breakevens are roughly 7,880 and 7,245 on the S&P.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus FY2028 GAAP EPS is a record of about $16.25 with no cuts, so the stock at $162.85 is roughly 10x that estimate and the cheapest of the AI era.
tension_points.bear_case: The stock is down 12% YTD with an RSI of 24, 14 banks are cutting targets, and this is the first print under an interim CEO.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Estimates coming down after the Tuesday 11/17 print would close the gap from the other side.
